scope: Internal assessment of an implemented sandbox hackathon prototype, not an official Devpost result or prediction of prizes.

criteria.name: Technological Implementation
criteria.reason: Substantial working sandbox integration: retained provider records show sponsor capture and donor refund, active subscription, paid invoice and verified duplicate-safe webhook, plus two-leg checkout and separate restart evidence. Current rehearsal imports and executes the actual call service, consent gate, claim checker and receipt builder with fresh isolated mock dependencies; source and behavioral tests cover changed terms, no consent, refused funding and uncertain outcomes. The cancellation policy repair still proposes an action and requires separate consent. The AI quality evidence remains mixed and does not earn credit as a fully passed intelligent workflow.

criteria.name: Design
criteria.reason: The inspected native desktop and phone complete states have a coherent visual identity, strong outcome hierarchy and unusually clear financial semantics. Sponsor amount, unresolved donor refund and active subscription appear together on the phone; the conversation disclosure reduces initial reading load. Native controls, visible focus treatment, semantic status output and explicit simulation/fee labels support a practical prototype experience. The large hero and long desktop conversation still contribute to the presentation friction captured in deduction D3; no usability-study result is inferred.

criteria.name: Potential Impact
criteria.reason: The primary workflow addresses a concrete recurring-donor hardship and after-hours support need, with a plausible mechanism for helping the donor while preserving an active gift. Sponsor-first execution and inspectable uncertainty are meaningful safeguards for the proposed audience. The packet carefully bounds sector statistics to their panels, but no independent donor/nonprofit observation, sponsor uptake or measured time saving, retention, or willingness to pay establishes realized benefit. This limits demonstrated impact rather than requiring production deployment or a formal independent study.

criteria.name: Innovation/Idea
criteria.reason: The combination of conversational supported-action completion, sponsor-backed hardship relief, fresh exact consent, provider readback, sentence-level evidence and a verifiable signed record is a distinctive and coherent prototype idea. Credit is for the implemented combination, not a first-ever claim. Conventional donor management already exists, controlled supplier endpoints do not establish an independent marketplace, and failed purchase-drafting/price comparisons do not establish an AI-specific procurement advantage. The fresh routing comparison supplies narrow semantic evidence, with its failed gate preserved.

criteria.name: Presentation
criteria.reason: The 73-second lead narrative has a clear problem, sponsor-first success, two blocked-write cases, an unresolved refund, and a separate retained actual receipt plus tamper rejection. Captions and provenance explicitly distinguish mock rehearsal, actual historical sandbox evidence and app-key integrity. The anonymous rehearsal lets a judge inspect current logic and varying amounts. Dense conversation text in the film frames, a large landing hero ahead of the video, and several historical recordings/procurement evidence paths impose some navigation and reading cost. Full motion, audio quality and timing were not independently watched, so they are not certified by this assessment.

materialDeductions.finding: AI assistance has not consistently met its own task gates: fresh donor routing was 11/12 versus rules 6/12, but failed for one wrong mutation route; the separate exposed-case policy repair is not a fresh model win. Purchase drafting was 11/24 versus rules 14/24, and negotiation does not demonstrate AI-specific savings.
materialDeductions.improvement: Keep the recorded failures explicit and support any stronger AI advantage claim with a new frozen evaluation of the current composed behavior.

materialDeductions.finding: A plausible donor-care mechanism and audience context are established, but independent target-user benefit and sponsor economics or uptake are unmeasured. Sector statistics alone cannot establish this app's effect.
materialDeductions.improvement: Obtain a small set of independent donor/nonprofit workflow observations and a concrete sponsor-fee/eligibility assessment before claiming realized impact.

materialDeductions.finding: Judge-facing evidence still has reading and navigation friction: the native demo screenshot places the movie controls near the viewport bottom after a large hero, film frames contain dense small conversation text, and several earlier recordings and procurement histories remain available on the same evidence page.
materialDeductions.improvement: Make the existing primary donor-relief film and interactive rehearsal easier to reach and keep the optional historical evidence compact; emphasize the existing outcome amounts and scope labels when narrating dense frames.

evidenceSeparation.simulation: Six bounded rules-routed scenarios execute current application logic against disposable mock PayPal and an in-memory ledger. No external calls, model-quality evidence, production persistence or microphone validation is established by these scenarios.
evidenceSeparation.actualProviderRecords: Retained JSON records report real PayPal sandbox actions and authenticated readbacks: donor pause/resume and relief, paid invoice/webhook, historical 676.25 USD checkout with restart and later separate 674.15 USD checkout without a newly injected restart. Test funds, one owned sandbox merchant and controlled suppliers; no independent fulfillment or live settlement is inferred.
evidenceSeparation.failedEvaluations: Original fresh donor-routing gate remains failed; cancellation policy regression coverage is a separate repair. Failed purchase drafting and AI price comparisons remain failed. Historical routing results do not replace current fresh validation.
evidenceSeparation.testSuite: Packet reports 1025 total, 1016 passing, 9 optional integration skips and zero failures, using mocks. Reviewer inspected relevant test source but did not rerun the suite or independently inspect its raw log.

viewLimits: Inspected six required still images at original resolution and read exact captions/provenance; did not watch the full movie in motion or listen to narration/audio.
No browsing, app interaction, provider/API requests, credentials access, payment operations, user contact or test reruns occurred.
Hash matching establishes local artifact consistency, not independent re-verification of historical provider records or deployment status.
Impact and competitor context were assessed as bounded claims in the supplied packet; external sources were not reopened under the review-only constraint.
No prior subjective assessment or earlier packet was opened. The default agent-self-evaluation skill was absent at the checked paths; the supplied five-criterion rubric was used directly.
complianceStatusSeparateFromScore: Public YouTube upload, Devpost submission, updated public source release and full eligibility/rules verification are not established. These were not invented as five-criterion production requirements.
verdict: Strong and unusually inspectable sandbox prototype. Its execution safeguards and donor-relief presentation are stronger than its current evidence for dependable AI advantage and realized user benefit. This is a single internal assessment, not an official competition result.
